summary: Apply the injective σ; the scalar ∏ψ(det g) contributes |∏ψ(det g)|² = 1, a root of unity having absolute value 1, and the pairing is invariant under translation.

steps.claim: Since σ is injective, it suffices to prove the equality of the two pairings after applying σ.
steps.lean:
innerAt σ x y := σ.injective (by
  erw [map_smulₛₗ₂, LinearMap.map_smul, smul_smul, map_mul, map_mul, σ.apply_symm_apply, conj_mul',
    (isOfFinOrder _ (isOfFinOrder_prod_psi_det ..)).norm_eq_one]
  simp; with_unfolding_all exact congr(_ * $(smoothPairing_formTranslation ..)))

steps.claim: formAction g acts by the scalar c = ∏_i ψ_{w_i}(det g_i) times translation; the pairing is conjugate-linear (for σ⁻¹∘conj∘σ) in the first variable and linear in the second, so after applying σ the left side is conj(σc)·σc = |σc|² times σ of the pairing of the translates; since c has finite order (isOfFinOrder_prod_psi_det), |σc| = 1.
steps.lean:
erw [map_smulₛₗ₂, LinearMap.map_smul, smul_smul, map_mul, map_mul, σ.apply_symm_apply, conj_mul',
    (isOfFinOrder _ (isOfFinOrder_prod_psi_det ..)).norm_eq_one]

steps.claim: The pairing of the translates of x and y equals the pairing of x and y (smoothPairing_formTranslation: the smooth pairing is invariant under right translation).
